 Thiago Silva confirms last Libertadores: “I want to reach Montevideo” 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article 42-year-old defender confirms farewell to continental tournament, eyes comeback against Palmeiras and reaffirms dream of reaching the final in Montevideo 
 After the 2–1 defeat to Palmeiras at the Maracanã in the first leg of the Libertadores semifinals, defender Thiago Silva spoke from the heart in the mixed zone. At 42, the Fluminense captain confirmed that this is his last campaign in the continental competition and revealed that his pursuit of a place in the final is also driven by a desire to overcome the heartbreak of the 2008 final, when Fluminense finished runners-up to LDU after a penalty shootout at the Maracanã.
 OneFootball Videos
 Photo: MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images
 Despite the disappointing result at home, the defender made it clear that the squad would not give up and that his goal is to take the Laranjeiras club back to the tournament's final, which will be played in Montevideo this season.
 “I have absolutely no doubt. I think this is a different, important moment, definitely my last Libertadores. I want to put 2008 behind me. I don't want to go out now. I at least want to be in Montevideo, competing and having the chance to play in another final,” the captain said, taking a deep breath to hold back his emotions.
 To secure that coveted place in the final and pursue the title, Fluminense will need to overturn the São Paulo side's lead at Nubank Parque. Aware of the challenge, Thiago Silva stressed the importance of the squad's commitment to overcoming the obstacle in São Paulo.
 “We know the task isn't easy, but nothing is impossible for those who put in the right work,” the defender concluded.
